columns.name: parallax
columns.description: parallax, not corrected for the zero point

columns.name: pm ra
columns.description: proper motion in right ascension times cos(dec), mu_alpha*

columns.name: BP-RP
columns.description: Gaia BP minus RP colour, not corrected for extinction

columns.name: parallax-pm ra correlation
columns.description: correlation coefficient of the parallax and pm ra errors (parallax_pmra_corr)

columns.name: parallax-pm dec correlation
columns.description: correlation coefficient of the parallax and pm dec errors (parallax_pmdec_corr)

columns.name: pm ra-pm dec correlation
columns.description: correlation coefficient of the pm ra and pm dec errors (pmra_pmdec_corr)

columns.name: RUWE
columns.description: renormalised unit weight error of the astrometric solution (ruwe)

columns.name: astrometric parameters solved
columns.description: astrometric_params_solved: 31 is a five-parameter solution, 95 a six-parameter one

columns.name: effective wavenumber
columns.description: in inverse micrometres: nu_eff_used_in_astrometry, the colour a five-parameter solution used; empty for a six-parameter solution

columns.name: pseudocolour
columns.description: in inverse micrometres: pseudocolour, the colour a six-parameter solution estimated; empty for a five-parameter solution

columns.name: ecliptic latitude
columns.description: ecliptic latitude (ecl_lat), which the parallax zero point depends on

masks.rule: a star with RUWE of 1.4 or more, whose astrometric solution Gaia flags as poor, is dropped

reductions: Every star within 14.14 arcmin of the same adopted center as the SDSS photometry pack (RA 114.602, Dec +21.575): 1048 stars brighter than G = 17.5, of which 993 have RUWE below 1.4 and are kept. The circle is the SDSS pack's, so the two tables can be set side by side.
Stars fainter than G = 17.5 are left out: their proper-motion errors approach the cluster's own spread.
Gaia is not blind in the cluster's core, as SDSS is: its crowding limit is far higher, so the core is in this table.
Positions are rounded to 0.00001 degree (0.04 arcsec), parallaxes, proper motions, errors and magnitudes to 0.001.
The Gaia source ids are left out (a 64-bit id does not fit the table encoding); the query in the pack's manifest returns them, and the rows are in its order.

Version 1.1.0 adds eight columns to the same 993 rows, all stored to the step shown: the three error correlations, RUWE, the solution type, the effective wavenumber or pseudocolour (each empty for the other solution type), and the ecliptic latitude. Every earlier column is identical to version 1.0.0 (tests/fixtures/gaia-workflows/alignment.json holds its checksum).

queries: SELECT source_id, ra, dec, parallax, parallax_error, pmra, pmra_error, pmdec, pmdec_error, phot_g_mean_mag, bp_rp, parallax_pmra_corr, parallax_pmdec_corr, pmra_pmdec_corr, ruwe, astrometric_params_solved, nu_eff_used_in_astrometry, pseudocolour, ecl_lat FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source WHERE ruwe<1.4 AND phot_g_mean_mag<17.5 AND parallax IS NOT NULL AND pmra IS NOT NULL AND 1=CONTAINS(POINT('ICRS',ra,dec),CIRCLE('ICRS',114.602,21.575,0.2357023)) ORDER BY source_id
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source WHERE phot_g_mean_mag<17.5 AND 1=CONTAINS(POINT('ICRS',ra,dec),CIRCLE('ICRS',114.602,21.575,0.2357023))
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM gaiadr3.gaia_source WHERE ruwe<1.4 AND phot_g_mean_mag<17.5 AND 1=CONTAINS(POINT('ICRS',ra,dec),CIRCLE('ICRS',114.602,21.575,0.2357023))

citations.text: Gaia Collaboration, Vallenari et al. 2023, A&A 674, A1 (Gaia Data Release 3: summary of the content and survey properties)
Gaia Collaboration, Prusti et al. 2016, A&A 595, A1 (The Gaia mission)
Katz et al. 2023, A&A 674, A5 (Gaia DR3: properties and validation of the radial velocities)
Lindegren et al. 2021, A&A 649, A2 (Gaia EDR3: astrometric solution; the RUWE statistic and the parallax zero-point)

steps: Query Gaia DR3 for every star within 0.2357023 degree of the adopted center with RUWE below 1.4, G below 17.5 and a parallax and proper motion (978 five-parameter and 15 six-parameter solutions), ordered by source id. Version 1.1.0 re-queries the same rows with the correlations, RUWE, the solution type and the colour and latitude the zero point needs.
Count, in two further queries, the stars in the same circle with and without the RUWE cut, for the mask.
Encode as table-columns/1: each column a whole number of its step from an offset, int16 where the range fits.

assumptions: Parallaxes are not corrected for the zero point (about -0.017 mas on average, Lindegren et al. 2021); at the cluster's 0.3 mas that is a 6 percent effect on its distance, which a lesson that quotes a distance says. The kernel's per-star zero point (js/kernels/galactic/zeropoint.js) needs the added columns; the stored parallax is still the catalogue's.

validation.check: a proper-motion and parallax mixture finds a cluster of at least 100 members within 0.3 mas/yr and 0.15 mas of the literature's values
